title: Resumable fragment handshake and deferred tool execution acceptance
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: customers observe brittle integrations when large structured responses are emitted as streams and upstream parsing fails mid-stream (network blips, partial validation errors). Current platform supports streaming JSON envelopes and function/tool calls, but lacks a standardized resumable-fragment handshake and a clear contract for deferred or idempotent tool invocation when fragments are re-emitted or replayed. This ticket defines acceptance criteria and a small-scope PRD for: (1) a resumable fragment handshake protocol to anchor partial structured emissions, (2) semantics for deferred tool/function execution when fragments are ambiguous, and (3) clear error and observability signals for integrators and SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Resumable fragment handshake: every streamed structured response that contains a multi-fragment object must begin with a short immutable envelope (fragment_id, version, checksum, total_fragments_hint) that receivers can use to detect continuation vs. restart.
Fragments may be re-sent: the platform must allow idempotent re-emission of previously-sent fragments within a 60s window without triggering duplicate external tool invocations.

Deferred tool execution contract: when a tool/function call reference is emitted inside a fragment that may be replayed, the platform will emit a distinct tool-invocation intent frame containing: invocation_id, fragment_id, schema_hint, and idempotency_token. SDKs must surface a staging state ("intent") and only execute the callable once an explicit "CONFIRM" frame for that invocation_id is emitted.

Graceful fallback: if a fragment stream terminates unexpectedly (EOF or transport error), the platform will emit a terminal frame describing the reason (partial|aborted|retryable) and a replay token clients may use to re-request continuation from the same fragment_id.

Observable signals: every fragment handshake, confirm, and terminal frame must generate structured telemetry with fields: fragment_id, invocation_id (optional), client_request_id, server_timestamp, bytes_emitted, and terminal_reason; these must be queryable in Console within 1 hour of emission.

Backpressure and ordering: the runtime must enforce causal ordering inside a single fragment sequence (fragments for the same fragment_id delivered in order) and support per-connection max-inflight fragments configurable at the route level.

Error modes: define three canonical error classes communicated in terminal frames and SDKs: recoverable_retryable, recoverable_resume_from_fragment, unrecoverable (schema mismatch). Each class maps to a recommended client action in docs.

Testing harness: e2e tests that inject transport interruptions, duplicate fragment delivery, and delayed CONFIRM frames must show no duplicated external tool side-effects in 99/100 runs using the idempotency_token mechanism.

Backward compatibility: if the client does not understand the handshake envelope (older SDK), the server will fall back to existing streaming behavior but include a warning header and log a deprecation metric for the route.

Docs and SDKs: release notes, JS and Python SDKs updated to expose: fragment events, confirm/intent lifecycle, replay_token usage, and helper utilities to implement confirm-once semantics. Examples for common patterns (long-form generation with tool calls, chunked JSON arrays) included in the PRD.
Rollout plan: canary rollout to 10% of hosted routes for 48h, metrics monitored (duplicate_invokes_rate < 0.01%, fragment_error_rate reduced by >= 30% for affected customers) before 100% rollout.
test_plan: Unit tests for handshake envelope encoding/decoding (fragment_id, checksum, total_fragments_hint)
Simulated network partition test: break connection mid-stream, re-establish, verify replay_token resumes stream and no duplicate tool execution
Chaos test: random duplicate fragment injection; assert idempotency_token prevents duplicate side-effects
SDK integration tests: JS/Python verify confirm-once lifecycle and surface terminal_reason to caller
Load test: ensure per-route max-inflight fragments prevents head-of-line blocking under bursty traffic
Telemetry verification: events appear in Console and match schema; sample dashboard receives entries within 1 hour
notes: Decision log: prefer explicit CONFIRM frame over optimistic auto-execute to avoid accidental double-invocation of tools (trade-off: more chattiness vs. correctness).
Trade-offs: implementing resumable fragments increases envelope bytes per stream (~+0.5% payload) but reduces integration breakages by avoiding ambiguous partial objects.
Security: idempotency_token must be cryptographically random; KMS not required for token generation but must be logged in telemetry as hashed value.
Related work: runtime batching changes (ENG-19902) may affect ordering guarantees; coordinate with eng lead to ensure per-fragment ordering semantics are preserved.
UX: Console will show a small visualization of fragment timelines for a request - initial mock attached below.
